questions.stem: A 67-year-old man has 4 months of fatigue. He has no bleeding and takes no medicines. The spleen is not palpable. His results are: hemoglobin 9.0 g/dL, hematocrit 27%, mean corpuscular volume 88 fL, reticulocyte count 3% (reference 0.5-1.5%), LDH normal, indirect bilirubin normal and haptoglobin normal. After the reticulocyte count is corrected for the degree of anemia, which mechanism best explains his anemia?
choices: Extravascular hemolysis in the spleen
Intravascular hemolysis with hemoglobin lost in the urine
Recent hemorrhage with an appropriate marrow response
Inadequate red cell production by the bone marrow
Short red cell survival from an inherited membrane defect
questions.explanation: The raw count looks high, but a low hematocrit means fewer red cells, so each reticulocyte is a larger percentage. Corrected count = 3 × (27 / 45) = **1.8%**, which is **below about 2%**: the marrow is **not responding enough**, so the anemia is **hypoproliferative**. Hemolysis is the most tempting choice because of the raw 3%, but normal LDH, indirect bilirubin and haptoglobin argue against it, and hemolysis would give a clearly high corrected count.
questions.explanation_pt: A contagem bruta parece alta, mas com hematócrito baixo há menos hemácias, então cada reticulócito representa uma porcentagem maior. Contagem corrigida = 3 × (27 / 45) = **1,8%**, **abaixo de cerca de 2%**: a medula **não está respondendo o suficiente**, então a anemia é **hipoproliferativa**. Hemólise é a opção mais tentadora por causa dos 3% brutos, mas LDH, bilirrubina indireta e haptoglobina normais falam contra ela, e a hemólise daria uma contagem corrigida claramente alta.

questions.stem: A 56-year-old woman has had rheumatoid arthritis for 12 years, with active swelling of the small joints of her hands. She has felt tired for 6 months. Stool tests for occult blood are negative. Her results are: hemoglobin 10.1 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume 79 fL, serum iron low, total iron-binding capacity low, transferrin saturation low, ferritin 420 ng/mL (high) and C-reactive protein high. Which mechanism best explains her anemia?
choices: Hepcidin-mediated breakdown of ferroportin
Chronic blood loss from NSAID-induced gastric erosions
Reduced synthesis of alpha-globin chains
Antibodies against red cell precursors in the marrow
Lack of a pyridoxine-dependent heme synthesis enzyme
questions.explanation: Chronic inflammation raises **IL-6**, which makes the liver release **hepcidin**. Hepcidin causes **ferroportin** to be internalized and degraded, so iron stays trapped in macrophages and enterocytes: **low serum iron**, **low TIBC** and **normal or high ferritin**. NSAID-related blood loss is the most tempting choice, but iron deficiency would give a **low ferritin** and a **high TIBC**, and her stool tests are negative.
questions.explanation_pt: A inflamação crônica aumenta a **IL-6**, que faz o fígado liberar **hepcidina**. A hepcidina faz a **ferroportina** ser internalizada e degradada, então o ferro fica retido nos macrófagos e enterócitos: **ferro sérico baixo**, **CTLF baixa** e **ferritina normal ou alta**. A perda sanguínea por AINE é a opção mais tentadora, mas a deficiência de ferro daria **ferritina baixa** e **CTLF alta**, e a pesquisa de sangue oculto nas fezes foi negativa.

questions.stem: A 74-year-old woman has 1 year of fatigue. In winter, her fingers, ears and the tip of her nose turn purple-blue, and her urine is sometimes dark after she spends time outdoors. She has had no recent infection. Hemoglobin is 9.4 g/dL. The reticulocyte count, LDH and indirect bilirubin are high, and haptoglobin is low. A blood smear made at room temperature shows large clumps of red cells, and the clumps disappear when the sample is warmed to 37°C. Which direct antiglobulin (Coombs) test result is most likely?
choices: Positive with anti-IgG, negative with anti-C3
Positive with both anti-IgG and anti-C3
Positive with anti-C3, negative with anti-IgG
Negative with both anti-IgG and anti-C3
Positive with anti-IgA, negative with anti-C3
questions.explanation: Cold-induced acrocyanosis and red cell clumping that disappears with warming point to **cold agglutinin disease**. **IgM** binds red cells in the cooler parts of the body and **fixes complement**, then falls off when the blood returns to core temperature; only **C3** stays on the cell, so the test is **positive for C3 only**. An IgG-positive test is the most tempting choice, but that pattern fits **warm AIHA**, which does not cause cold-triggered symptoms or agglutination.
questions.explanation_pt: Acrocianose induzida pelo frio e aglutinação das hemácias que desaparece com o aquecimento indicam **doença das aglutininas frias**. A **IgM** se liga às hemácias nas partes mais frias do corpo e **fixa complemento**, depois se solta quando o sangue volta à temperatura central; só o **C3** fica na célula, então o teste é **positivo apenas para C3**. Um teste positivo para IgG é a opção mais tentadora, mas esse padrão é o da **AHAI quente**, que não causa sintomas desencadeados pelo frio nem aglutinação.

questions.stem: A 48-year-old man is treated in the hospital with high-dose intravenous penicillin G for streptococcal endocarditis. On day 10 he becomes pale and tired. Hemoglobin has fallen from 13.2 to 9.0 g/dL. The reticulocyte count, LDH and indirect bilirubin are high. The direct antiglobulin test is positive with anti-IgG and negative with anti-C3. The smear shows spherocytes and no schistocytes. His anemia improves after penicillin is replaced by vancomycin. What is the most likely mechanism of his hemolysis?
choices: Drug-induced autoantibodies against Rh antigens
Oxidant damage to hemoglobin in cells with low NADPH
Fragmentation of red cells by the infected heart valve
Complement lysis by circulating drug-IgM complexes
IgG against penicillin bound to the red cell membrane
questions.explanation: High-dose **penicillin** binds the red cell membrane and acts as a **hapten**. IgG made against the drug coats the cells, and splenic macrophages remove them (**extravascular hemolysis**, spherocytes, IgG-positive Coombs test); it stops when the drug is stopped. Drug-induced Rh autoantibodies are the most tempting choice, but that is the classic **methyldopa** mechanism: it appears only after **months** of treatment, and the antibody reacts with red cells even without the drug. Drug-IgM immune complexes would fix complement and give a C3-positive test.
questions.explanation_pt: A **penicilina** em dose alta se liga à membrana da hemácia e funciona como **hapteno**. A IgG produzida contra o fármaco recobre as células, e os macrófagos do baço as removem (**hemólise extravascular**, esferócitos, Coombs positivo para IgG); o quadro cessa quando o fármaco é suspenso. Autoanticorpos anti-Rh induzidos por fármaco são a opção mais tentadora, mas esse é o mecanismo clássico da **metildopa**: surge apenas após **meses** de tratamento, e o anticorpo reage com as hemácias mesmo sem o fármaco. Imunocomplexos de fármaco com IgM fixariam complemento e dariam teste positivo para C3.

questions.stem: A 7-year-old boy is brought to the clinic because of easy bruising and frequent nosebleeds. He is short for his age, has several café-au-lait spots and was born without a right thumb. Hemoglobin is 8.1 g/dL with a mean corpuscular volume of 104 fL, white cell count is 2,600/µL and platelet count is 35,000/µL. The reticulocyte count is low. A bone marrow biopsy shows very few blood-forming cells, and most of the space is filled with fat. A defect in which cellular process is the most likely cause?
choices: Synthesis of ribosomal proteins in erythroid precursors
Repair of DNA interstrand cross-links
Attachment of GPI-anchored proteins to the cell surface
Repair of thymine dimers caused by ultraviolet light
Mismatch repair of errors made during DNA replication
questions.explanation: Pancytopenia with a **hypocellular, fatty marrow**, short stature, **thumb defects** and café-au-lait spots is **Fanconi anemia**, a usually autosomal recessive defect in the pathway that repairs **DNA interstrand cross-links**. Stem cells fail over time, and the risk of **AML** and squamous cell cancers is high; cells show many chromosome breaks when exposed to cross-linking agents. Diamond-Blackfan anemia (ribosomal protein defect) is the most tempting choice because it also causes thumb defects and macrocytosis, but it affects **only the red cell line**.
questions.explanation_pt: Pancitopenia com **medula hipocelular e gordurosa**, baixa estatura, **defeitos do polegar** e manchas café com leite indicam **anemia de Fanconi**, defeito geralmente autossômico recessivo na via que repara as **ligações cruzadas entre as fitas do DNA**. As células-tronco falham com o tempo, e o risco de **LMA** e de carcinomas espinocelulares é alto; as células mostram muitas quebras cromossômicas quando expostas a agentes que formam ligações cruzadas. A anemia de Diamond-Blackfan (defeito de proteína ribossômica) é a opção mais tentadora, pois também causa defeitos do polegar e macrocitose, mas afeta **apenas a linhagem eritroide**.

questions.stem: A 9-year-old girl has had anemia and mild jaundice since infancy, and her spleen is enlarged. Her parents are first cousins, and both have normal blood counts. Hemoglobin is 8.2 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume is 92 fL and the reticulocyte count is high. The direct antiglobulin test is negative, and osmotic fragility is normal. The smear shows some red cells with many small, regular spikes. Red cell testing shows low activity of the enzyme that converts phosphoenolpyruvate to pyruvate. She plays soccer and has fewer symptoms than expected for her hemoglobin level. Which change in her red cells best explains this?
choices: More HbF, which binds oxygen more tightly
Less 2,3-BPG, which shifts the curve to the left
More methemoglobin, which releases oxygen more easily
More 2,3-BPG, which shifts the curve to the right
More ATP, which keeps the red cells more flexible
questions.explanation: This is **pyruvate kinase deficiency**, an autosomal recessive cause of chronic **extravascular hemolysis**. The block at the end of glycolysis makes upstream intermediates build up, so red cells make more **2,3-BPG**; this **right shift** of the oxygen dissociation curve helps tissues get oxygen despite the anemia. Less 2,3-BPG is the most tempting choice, but that happens when glycolysis is blocked at an early step (for example, hexokinase deficiency). ATP is **low** in pyruvate kinase deficiency, which makes the cells rigid and easy for the spleen to remove.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **deficiência de piruvato quinase**, causa autossômica recessiva de **hemólise extravascular** crônica. O bloqueio no fim da glicólise faz os intermediários anteriores se acumularem, então as hemácias produzem mais **2,3-BPG**; esse **desvio para a direita** da curva de dissociação do oxigênio ajuda os tecidos a receber oxigênio apesar da anemia. Menos 2,3-BPG é a opção mais tentadora, mas isso ocorre quando a glicólise é bloqueada em uma etapa inicial (por exemplo, deficiência de hexoquinase). O ATP está **baixo** na deficiência de piruvato quinase, o que deixa as células rígidas e fáceis de remover pelo baço.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man had his aortic valve replaced with a mechanical valve 9 years ago, and he takes warfarin. He has 6 months of fatigue. A new early diastolic murmur is heard along the left sternal border, and echocardiography shows a leak around the valve ring. His results are: hemoglobin 9.6 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume 79 fL, reticulocyte count high, LDH 1,150 U/L (high), haptoglobin undetectable and ferritin low. The smear shows helmet cells and other red cell fragments. The urine dipstick is positive for blood, but urine microscopy shows no red cells. Stool tests for occult blood are negative, and upper endoscopy and colonoscopy last month were normal. What is the most likely cause of his low iron stores?
choices: Urinary loss of hemoglobin and hemosiderin iron
Hidden bleeding from the gut caused by warfarin
Iron trapped in splenic macrophages by hepcidin
Iron loss from frequent blood tests for INR monitoring
Low iron intake from a vitamin K-restricted diet
questions.explanation: Turbulent flow through the **paravalvular leak** tears red cells (schistocytes), causing chronic **intravascular hemolysis**. Free hemoglobin saturates haptoglobin and is filtered into the urine (**hemoglobinuria**: dipstick positive without red cells); tubular cells store some of it as **hemosiderin** and shed it, so iron leaves the body and **iron deficiency** develops. Gut bleeding on warfarin is the most tempting choice, but the stool tests and both endoscopies are negative. In extravascular hemolysis, macrophages recycle the iron, so iron is not lost.
questions.explanation_pt: O fluxo turbulento pelo **vazamento paravalvar** rompe as hemácias (esquizócitos), causando **hemólise intravascular** crônica. A hemoglobina livre satura a haptoglobina e é filtrada para a urina (**hemoglobinúria**: fita reagente positiva sem hemácias); as células tubulares armazenam parte dela como **hemossiderina** e a eliminam, então o ferro sai do corpo e surge **deficiência de ferro**. Sangramento gastrointestinal pela varfarina é a opção mais tentadora, mas a pesquisa de sangue oculto e as duas endoscopias foram negativas. Na hemólise extravascular, os macrófagos reciclam o ferro, então ele não é perdido.

questions.stem: A 23-year-old man has 2 months of numbness in his feet and an unsteady gait that is worse in the dark. For the past year he has inhaled nitrous oxide from small gas cartridges almost every day at parties. He eats a mixed diet that includes meat. Exam shows loss of vibration and position sense in the legs and a positive Romberg sign. Hemoglobin is 11.0 g/dL and mean corpuscular volume is 108 fL; the smear shows hypersegmented neutrophils. Serum vitamin B12 is in the low-normal range, and methylmalonic acid and homocysteine are both high. What is the mechanism of his disease?
choices: Inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase
Lack of intrinsic factor from parietal cell loss
Malabsorption of B12 in the terminal ileum
Blocked pyrimidine synthesis at UMP synthase
Oxidation of cobalamin, which makes it inactive
questions.explanation: **Nitrous oxide** oxidizes the **cobalt** atom in cobalamin, so B12 can no longer work as a cofactor. The result is a **functional B12 deficiency**: high **methylmalonic acid** and **homocysteine**, megaloblastic anemia and **subacute combined degeneration**, even when the measured serum B12 is not low. Pernicious anemia is the most tempting choice, but this young man has a clear toxic exposure and no clue of autoimmune gastritis. Dihydrofolate reductase inhibition (methotrexate) raises homocysteine but leaves methylmalonic acid normal.
questions.explanation_pt: O **óxido nitroso** oxida o átomo de **cobalto** da cobalamina, então a B12 deixa de funcionar como cofator. O resultado é uma **deficiência funcional de B12**: **ácido metilmalônico** e **homocisteína** altos, anemia megaloblástica e **degeneração combinada subaguda**, mesmo quando a B12 sérica medida não está baixa. A anemia perniciosa é a opção mais tentadora, mas este jovem tem uma exposição tóxica clara e nenhum indício de gastrite autoimune. A inibição da di-hidrofolato redutase (metotrexato) eleva a homocisteína, mas deixa o ácido metilmalônico normal.
